id: D50-0 gate: do explicit electron-pressure features from the Thomson pulses carry what the heads miss?
author: first_agent
entrant: 2026-10-13: continue; small confirmed gains count; honesty is rule zero
observation: Public board 2026-10-13 by component: our q95/betaN term .99789 is the lowest of the first ten (5th place .9983; 9th and 14th also .9983 with a worse boundary than ours). D49 (measurement): the heads are calibrated (slope of truth on prediction 1.00), the last frame of a record holds about 10 % of the squared error of either head over 5936 shots; no shrink or regime fix is available. The networks read electron temperature and density separately, as 8 cm bin means of the one pulse nearest to the frame (features.py, shot_reader._resample), with window means over whole frames only. No pressure product, no chord integral of it, no ratio to field and current, no mean over the two or three pulses inside a frame.
question: Does a cross-fitted residual corrector that reads thermal features (pressure integrals along the vertical laser, their means over +-10 ms, +-50 ms, 150 ms and 500 ms before the frame, and their ratios to toroidal-field current x plasma current, current squared and field squared) reduce the out-of-fold head error more than the same corrector without them?

arms.control: 13 out-of-fold S16 heads + plasma current, toroidal-field current, their ratio, 1/current

data: nn_oof.npz of D9-0 (sha 'nn_oof' below): 5936 non-reserved training shots, 1 317 704 frames, five folds; DIII-D training data only, inputs only for the features
corrector: D10-0 settings: xgboost hist, depth 6, eta .03, subsample .8, colsample .5, min_child_weight 50, lambda 5, 4000 rounds, patience 150, seed 10; CPU (xgboost 3.4.1) instead of the Kaggle GPU; fit on three folds, stop on a fourth, predict the fifth; both arms in the same process
measure: d50_paired.py: each arm blended into the heads as in d9_gate_eval.py (nested least-squares weight in [0,1]); head proxy of the score change (d9_gate_eval.proxy); treatment minus control on the same 2000 shot resamples, seed 990
rule: PASS if paired dS_proxy >= +1.5e-5 with P >= .95 and positive in at least four folds. PASS -> the thermal features go into the networks' own table: a paired network arm in the manner of D18-0 (same members, seeds and settings with and without the columns), then a production refit only if that passes. FAIL -> the heads already extract what the Thomson pressure carries; closed. Per-target differences are reported whatever the outcome and do not admit anything by themselves.
known_limits: The out-of-fold heads are those of the 16-network table ensemble of 5 Oct, not the deployed 69 networks with sub-frame inputs: a gain here is an upper indication for the deployed heads, not a measurement on them. The control arm is compact (no 367-column table); D10-0 with the whole table found nothing (-2e-6).
exposure: Before the freeze: extractor smoke test on the first 20 training shots (inputs), and on those 20 shots the correlation of the ratio columns with the betaN label (.64 to .92) as a check that the columns are what they claim. No corrector fitted. The 5936 shots' out-of-fold heads were used by D9, D10, D12, D14, D15, D16, D24 gates.
